security_audit.summary: Static command-execution and reconnaissance findings are false positives from Markdown tool names, parameters, and workflow notes. The hardcoded URL is a documented Rube MCP setup endpoint, not hidden exfiltration. Semantic review found sensitive Wrike operations that can delete content or change workspace access.

remediation.issue: Wrike delete workflows can permanently remove folders, spaces, and related content.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation with exact IDs and names before WRIKE_DELETE_FOLDER or WRIKE_DELETE_SPACE.

remediation.issue: Wrike invitations and sharing changes can grant workspace or folder access.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm recipient email, role, target folder, and workspace scope before access changes.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on a third-party MCP endpoint for Wrike automation.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to verify the Rube MCP endpoint and review Wrike OAuth scopes before connecting.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Wrike connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `wrike`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
2. `WRIKE_GET_ALL_CUSTOM_FIELDS` - Get custom field IDs if needed [Optional]
- `folderId`: Parent folder ID where the task will be created
- `responsibles`: Array of user IDs to assign
- `dates`: Object with type, start, due, duration
- `folderId`: Parent folder ID for creation; target folder ID for modification
- `customItemTypeId`: Set to create as a project instead of a folder
- `shareds`: Array of user IDs or emails to share with
- `project`: Filter for projects (true) or folders (false) in GET_FOLDERS
2. `WRIKE_GET_TASK_BY_ID` - Get detailed info for a specific task [Optional]
- `taskId`: Specific task ID for detailed retrieval
- `resolve_user_names`: Auto-resolve user IDs to names (default true)
2. `WRIKE_LIST_SPACE_TASK_BLUEPRINTS` - List blueprints in a specific space [Alternative]
- `task_blueprint_id`: ID of the blueprint to launch
3. `WRIKE_CREATE_INVITATION` - Invite a user to the workspace [Optional]
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Either parent_id or super_task_id is required, not both
- Custom email subjects/messages require a paid Wrike plan
2. Find field by name, extract id and type
| Launch blueprint | WRIKE_LAUNCH_TASK_BLUEPRINT_ASYNC | task_blueprint_id, title, parent_id |

content.user_title: Automate Wrike Projects with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Wrike project updates can be repetitive and error prone when IDs, custom fields, and permissions are involved. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows for reliable Wrike automation.
actual_capabilities: Searches Rube MCP for current Wrike tool schemas before workflow execution.
Creates and modifies Wrike tasks with assignees, status, importance, dates, and custom fields.
Creates, updates, lists, and deletes Wrike folders and projects.
Fetches Wrike tasks by filters or task ID with pagination guidance.
Launches Wrike task blueprints and manages spaces, contacts, and invitations.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active Wrike OAuth connection.
Cannot guess Wrike IDs; folders, users, tasks, and fields must be resolved first.
Wrike permissions and plan features may block some operations.
Destructive actions need explicit user confirmation before execution.

use_cases.title: Create Assigned Project Tasks
use_cases.description: Create Wrike tasks with owners, due dates, importance, status, and custom field values.

use_cases.title: Organize Team Workspaces
use_cases.description: Build or update Wrike folders, projects, shared access, and subfolder structures.

use_cases.title: Track Work and Launch Templates
use_cases.description: Fetch filtered tasks, inspect details, and launch approved task blueprints from Wrike.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Wrike Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Wrike task in the correct folder for this work item. Resolve the folder and assignee IDs first, then summarize the created task.

prompt_templates.title: Update Project Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the target Wrike project, list its subfolders, and create any missing folders I describe. Ask before deleting or moving existing content.

prompt_templates.title: Review Active Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch active Wrike tasks due this week for the selected project. Resolve user names and group the results by assignee and due date.

prompt_templates.title: Launch a Blueprint Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: List available Wrike task blueprints, confirm the selected blueprint and parent location, then launch it with the requested title and schedule.

output_examples.input: Create a high priority onboarding task for Jordan due Friday.
output_examples.output: The assistant resolves the folder and Jordan user ID, creates the task, and reports title, assignee, status, priority, and due date.

output_examples.input: Show open tasks in the product launch project.
output_examples.output: The assistant finds the project, fetches active tasks with pagination, and summarizes owners, due dates, statuses, and important blockers.

output_examples.input: Launch the campaign checklist blueprint for next month.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists matching blueprints, asks for confirmation, launches the selected blueprint, and explains when tasks may appear.

best_practices: Search Rube MCP tools before each workflow so schemas match the current connector.
Resolve folder, task, field, and user IDs before creating or updating Wrike records.
Confirm destructive actions, invitations, and sharing changes with exact target details.
anti_patterns: Do not guess Wrike IDs from names or examples.
Do not delete folders, spaces, or tasks without explicit confirmation.
Do not invite users or change sharing without checking email, role, and scope.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Wrike API key?
faq.answer: No direct API key is listed. It requires Rube MCP and an active Wrike OAuth connection.

faq.question: Can it create Wrike tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides task creation after resolving the target folder and assignee IDs.

faq.question: Can it manage custom fields?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs the assistant to fetch custom field definitions before setting values.

faq.question: Can it delete Wrike content?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents delete operations, so users should require explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Does it support blueprints?
faq.answer: Yes. It can list task blueprints and launch a selected blueprint asynchronously.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
